subject: Food Science
title: Calcium and Bone Health
description: One-minute skill: Calcium and Bone Health.

hook.text: Your skeleton rebuilds every 10 years. After 30, breakdown outpaces rebuilding—calcium intake determines bone loss speed.

buildup.text: Calcium is the most abundant mineral in the body—99% stored in bones and teeth. The remaining 1% runs muscles and nerves.

discovery.text: Peak bone mass is reached by age 30. After that, you're making withdrawals. Higher peak mass means a bigger reserve for aging.

twist.text: Countries with most dairy (Scandinavia) have highest fracture rates. Calcium alone won't prevent osteoporosis—exercise matters.

climax.text: Non-dairy sources: kale, broccoli, sardines, fortified OJ, and tofu set with calcium sulfate. Dairy isn't the only option.

punchline.text: Build bone before 30. Maintain it after. Calcium helps—but so does exercise.

quiz.question: When does peak bone mass occur?
options: By age 30—after that, bone breakdown outpaces rebuilding
